extraSuggestedThemes.name: Collected Vintage Cabin
extraSuggestedThemes.whyItFits: Suits this house because the wood beam, wood doors, and existing hardwood already give it history. It stays cosmetic, avoids blue, and is naturally budget-friendly.
extraSuggestedThemes.sourceSays: Houzz’s Fall 2026 report (September 2, 2026) says collected, layered interiors are taking hold, with homeowners favoring character, vintage pieces, and personal storytelling over off-the-shelf perfection. A public search summary of BHG’s 2026 thrifted-and-vintage piece points to vintage lighting, layered collected objects, and functional storage furniture such as hutches.
extraSuggestedThemes.interpretation: A whole-house look built on dirty-neutral or khaki walls, kept wood, thrifted lamps and tables, and a few inherited or secondhand textiles would be the budget path. It overlaps slightly with English Cottage but is less floral and more about found objects than heritage paint.

extraSuggestedThemes.name: Hollywood Cottage
extraSuggestedThemes.whyItFits: A polished cream-and-linen alternative to English Cottage. It would feel collected and comfortable without plum or dusty rose, and it avoids blue.
extraSuggestedThemes.sourceSays: Brit + Co’s 2026 home-decor trends piece describes a ‘Hollywood Cottage’ look and attributes the name to Shea McGee, calling it cozy yet sophisticated, in the Nancy Meyers vein.
extraSuggestedThemes.interpretation: For this house that would mean cream walls, white ceilings, mid oak in the carpeted rooms, simple slipcovered or linen-look furnishings later, and brass in small amounts. It is calmer than Moody Lodge and more dressed than Scandi Cabin.

sourceSays: Homes & Gardens (December 27, 2025) reports designers still expect dark paints in 2026, with interest shifting toward jewel tones, near-black olives, burgundy, and warm-toned blacks rather than navy, and toward color-drenching in small or intimate rooms. Designers also say a home needs both dark and light rooms for balance, and that lighter accessories can keep a dark scheme livable.

Apartment Therapy’s mid-2026 ‘still in’ list, as indexed, includes colorful and color-drenched rooms, with charcoal, espresso browns, and aubergines among the hues designers name. Bill wants white ceilings, so these looks do not drench the ceiling.
Benjamin Moore’s 2026 Color of the Year, Silhouette AF-655 (announced October 16, 2025), is described by the company as rich espresso hues with subtle notes of charcoal.
Behr’s 2027 Color of the Year, Grounded T27-01 (announced August 26, 2026), is an earthy olive with brown undertones.
trends.interpretation: Moody Lodge uses the near-black olive and espresso those sources actually describe, keeps ceilings white per Bill’s preference, and uses a light 3rd bedroom so the dark rooms have somewhere to contrast.
trends.onABudget: Paint is the main spend: dark olive in the living room and kitchen, espresso in the office, a slightly lighter olive in the master. Swap the two carpets for a mid-tone vinyl plank. Add aged-brass-look knobs and a faucet from a big-box or IKEA aisle, and later a thrifted leather chair or rust throw. Do not recast the existing hardwood until a later, measured decision.

sourceSays: Sherwin-Williams’ 2026 Color of the Year is Universal Khaki SW 6150, which the company describes as a mid-tone neutral with a slight yellow undertone, chosen for livability and longevity.
Houzz’s Fall 2026 report says warmth is now a baseline: layered warm wood tones, earthy colors, and natural materials, rather than stark white-and-gray rooms.
House Beautiful’s dirty-neutrals piece describes designers moving away from stark white toward earthier neutrals such as mushroom, greige, cognac, and olive.

Pinterest Predicts 2026 (December 9, 2025) includes Neo Deco, described as geometric Art Deco forms edged in chrome or brass, after years of heavy minimalism. That is a related, not identical, mid-century-adjacent brass-and-geometry trend.
trends.interpretation: Khaki as the field color is taken from the Sherwin-Williams 2026 COTY. Mustard, rust, and a walnut-look bedroom floor are this look’s mid-century reading of Houzz’s warm woods and earthy colors, not a claim that those sources specified this exact scheme.
trends.onABudget: Paint the main rooms khaki, the island mustard, and the office rust. Use brass-look knobs and a faucet from Target, IKEA, or a hardware aisle. Put a walnut-look vinyl in the two carpeted bedrooms. Later, add one or two walnut-toned or tapered-leg pieces from a thrift store rather than a matched mid-century suite.

sourceSays: Houzz’s Fall 2026 report describes a continued move away from stark white-and-gray, and toward warmth, texture, and natural materials. A lighter Scandi scheme therefore needs a warm white, not a cool gallery white, to stay in step with that baseline.

Apartment Therapy’s mid-2026 list also includes ‘warm minimalism’: richer wood tones and tactile materials that ‘balance restraint with character,’ as quoted from designer Cody Brown in search-indexed coverage of that article.

Sherwin-Williams’ 2027 Color of the Year, Celery SW 6421, is described as a soft, muted green with subtle yellow undertones. It is a related light, nature-connected direction, but it is not used as a wall color here so this look stays clearly distinct from the green rooms in Moody Lodge and in the earlier Northwoods Lake look.
trends.interpretation: Scandi Cabin is the restrained, light end of the same warm-materials story, with black used only as hardware. It is an interpretation, not a named 2026 ‘Scandi Cabin’ trend in these sources.
trends.onABudget: A few gallons of warm white, pale vinyl plank in the two carpeted bedrooms, and matte-black IKEA or big-box hardware and a matching faucet do most of the work. Keep furnishings sparse. Linen-look bedding and one pale wood or black lamp from Target or IKEA are enough later staging.

sourceSays: Homes & Gardens’ English-cottage color piece says designers are using muted, earthy heritage hues again, including dusty rose and muted greens, and are moving from gray-and-white rooms toward moody, earthy palettes. The same piece mentions duck-egg blue, which is not used here.
Valspar’s 2026 Color of the Year, Warm Eucalyptus 8004-28F (announced August 7, 2025), is described by the company as a grounded green inspired by vintage design palettes, with warm undertones.
Apartment Therapy’s mid-2026 coverage, as indexed, names aubergines among colors used in color-drenched rooms.
Benjamin Moore’s 2026 Color Trends palette, announced with Silhouette on October 16, 2025, includes Swiss Coffee OC-45 and First Crush CSP-310 among the complementary hues.
trends.interpretation: Cream, dusty rose, muted sage, and plum are this look’s reading of those heritage and aubergine notes, with blue deliberately left out. Vacant renders do not show floral textiles; those would be a later staging layer.
trends.onABudget: Paint is again the lever: cream in the main rooms, rose in the master, sage in the 3rd bedroom, plum in the office and on the island. Antique-brass-look hardware from a hardware aisle, honey vinyl in the two carpeted rooms, and later a few thrifted floral pillows, a vintage lamp, or mismatched frames, which lines up with the thrift-and-collected direction in Houzz and in the BHG 2026 vintage summary.

sourceSays: Houzz’s Fall 2026 report emphasizes warmth, wood, and natural materials as a baseline, and character over perfection. A black-and-wood scheme that keeps the existing oak and the wood beam sits inside that baseline rather than returning to cool gray-and-white minimalism.

Pinterest Predicts 2026 describes Neo Deco as geometric forms edged in chrome or brass. Matte black hardware is not what that report specifies; it is this look’s simpler, more widely available finish.

Homes & Gardens (December 27, 2025) notes designers favoring warm-toned blacks among the dark colors expected to continue, and also notes dark color used on a kitchen island as a way to add drama without committing every wall.
trends.interpretation: The black island is the one clearly dramatic move, which matches the ‘dark color on an island’ idea from that Homes & Gardens piece. The rest of the house stays a warm white so the existing wood can read as the other half of the scheme.
trends.onABudget: Warm white paint, a quart or two of matte black for the island, black IKEA or Home Depot hardware and a black faucet, and a mid-tone vinyl in the two carpeted bedrooms. Leave the existing hardwood and the wood beam alone. This is one of the cheaper looks to stage later, because the furniture can stay simple.
